## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
After a scheduled power down of the SynologyDSM server, at startup, none of the entities/devices are seen, and all show as 'unavailable'
This has always worked flawlessly, up to at least 115.
Since we cant 'reload' the integration (shouldn't this be available on all core integrations?), all we can do is restart the instance.

- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): OS

comments:
Hey there @hacf-fr, @quentame, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`synology_dsm`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L435) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

small but important update:
I've now noticed there is a 'reload' option available, but this is while none of the entities are unavailable. 

Could it have been the complete integration lost 'contact' with the system, and as a consequence, both the settings in the UI/integrations and the devices/entities were 'unavailable'?

Hi !

Are you having the same logs as #41589 ?

Solving #41589 is different because it's at config setup, but here the config is already set up.

In 116 we just added the Surveillance Station support, so shouldn't be much different.

If you have time to check this out, I'll appreciate your PR, because I'm currently busy on `icloud`, other `synology_dsm` issues.

Otherwise I'll check in few weeks.

review_comments: Don't patch the core. Set up the integration and check that the services are registered in the service registry.

Don't interact with integration details in the tests.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/development_testing#writing-tests-for-integrations

Why adding `SynologyDSMLoginFailedException` here ?

I think `SynologyDSMRequestException` should be enough.

same here
> because during boot (after reboot or scheduled downtime) DSM it self is already reachable (no connection error), but still login is unavailable (login failed) because DSM says "still booting, please try later"

just to be sure: register the same service multiple times causes no issue ?

(when multiple NAS)

during tests with two configured DSM:

- async_register() is called twice per service
- but when service is triggered/used it is only processed once

so I would assume there is something like "when service already exists, do not register again" ans therefore I assume no problems 😃
This test should not be part of the config flow tests. It should move to a `test_init.py` module.
Logging the services we register seems not needed. There's no variation.
Why do we not await this executor job?
I think here : `hass.data[DOMAIN][entry.unique_id]`, we should add a comment to say "Unique ID should be serial for integration services" (also in config_flow ?)
sorry, but not sure if i get it 😕 could you explain a little bit more or provide an example?

When we set `entry.unique_id` (config flow: `await self.async_set_unique_id(serial, raise_on_progress=False)`) and save it to the data (init `hass.data[DOMAIN][entry.unique_id] = {`), I think we should add a comment to precise the unique_id should be the serial (to prevent future changes).


```python
    # unique_id should be serial for services purpose
    hass.data[DOMAIN][entry.unique_id] = {
        SYNO_API: api,
        UNDO_UPDATE_LISTENER: undo_listener,
    }
```
ah yeah ... now I get it and fully agree ... have added the comment in config_flow, because there `unique_id` is set
Please only wrap the line that can raise in the try... except block.
Max debug level.

Why adding `SynologyDSMLoginFailedException` here ?

I think `SynologyDSMRequestException` should be enough.

because during boot (_after reboot or scheduled downtime_) DSM it self is already reachable (_no connection error_), but still login is unavailable (_login failed_) because DSM says "still booting, please try later"
We start logging messages with capital letter.
We don't need to copy exceptions to string when logging them. They have a `__str__` magic method already.
This is already logged by the core.
